arxiv-2205-10557.title: Electric Current Induced by Microwave Stark Effect of Electrons on Liquid Helium
arxiv-2205-10557.creator: T. Wang, M. Zhang, L. F. Wei
arxiv-2205-10557.description: Abstract We propose a frequency-mixed effect of Terahertz (THz) and Gigahertz (GHz) electromagnetic waves in the cryogenic system of electrons floating on liquid helium surface. The THz wave is near-resonant with the transition frequency between the lowest two levels of surface state electrons.

arxiv-2208-05028.title: Striped Ultradilute Liquid of Dipolar Bosons in Two Dimensions
arxiv-2208-05028.creator: Clemens Staudinger 1 , Diana Hufnagl 2,3 , Ferran Mazzanti 4 and Robert E. Zillich 1
arxiv-2208-05028.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Clemens Staudinger 1 , Diana Hufnagl 2,3 , Ferran Mazzanti 4 and Robert E. Zillich 1. We investigate the phases of a Bose-Einstein condensate of dipolar atoms restricted to move in a two-dimensional plane. The dipole moments are all aligned in a direction tilted with respect to the plane normal. As a result of the attractive and repulsive components of the dipole-dipole interaction, the dipolar gas has a self-bound phase, which is stabilized by quantum fluctuations.

arxiv-2210-14151.title: Drastically Reducing the Number of Trainable Parameters in Deep CNNs by Inter-layer Kernel-sharing
arxiv-2210-14151.creator: Alireza Azadbakht 1, Saeed Reza Kheradpisheh 1,, Ismail Khalfaoui-Hassani 2, Timothée Masquelier 3
arxiv-2210-14151.description: Abstract Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have become the state-of-the-art (SOTA) approach for many computer vision tasks: image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation, etc. However, most SOTA networks are too large for edge computing. Here, we suggest a simple way to reduce the number of trainable parameters and thus the memory footprint: sharing kernels between multiple convolutional layers.

arxiv-2302-05603.title: Solvable Dynamics of Coupled High-Dimensional Generalized Limit-Cycle Oscillators
arxiv-2302-05603.creator: Wei Zou 1, Sujuan He 1, D.V. Senthilkumar 2, Jürgen Kurths 3,4
arxiv-2302-05603.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wei Zou 1, Sujuan He 1, D.V. Senthilkumar 2, Jürgen Kurths 3,4. We introduce a new model consisting of globally coupled high-dimensional generalized limit-cycle oscillators, which explicitly incorporates the role of amplitude dynamics of individual units in the collective dynamics. In the limit of weak coupling, our model reduces to the D D -dimensional Kuramoto phase model, akin to a similar classic construction of the well-known Kuramoto phase model from weakly coupled two-dimensional limit-cycle oscillators.

arxiv-2304-10867.title: Application of quantum-inspired generative models to small molecular datasets
arxiv-2304-10867.creator: Charles Moussa, Hao Wang, Mauricio Araya-Polo, Thomas Bäck, Vedran Dunjko
arxiv-2304-10867.description: Abstract Quantum and quantum-inspired machine learning has emerged as a promising and challenging research field due to the increased popularity of quantum computing, especially with near-term devices. Theoretical contributions point toward generative modeling as a promising direction to realize the first examples of real-world quantum advantages from these technologies.

arxiv-2305-18354.title: LLMs and the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus: Successes, Failures, and the Importance of Object-based Representations
arxiv-2305-18354.creator: Yudong Xu wil.xu@mail.utoronto.ca, Wenhao Li chriswenhao.li@mail.utoronto.ca, Pashootan Vaezipoor pashootan@cs.toronto.edu, Scott Sanner ssanner@mie.utoronto.ca, Elias B. Khalil khalil@mie.utoronto.ca
arxiv-2305-18354.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yudong Xu wil.xu@mail.utoronto.ca, Wenhao Li chriswenhao.li@mail.utoronto.ca, Pashootan Vaezipoor pashootan@cs.toronto.edu, Scott Sanner ssanner@mie.utoronto.ca, Elias B. Khalil khalil@mie.utoronto.ca. Can a Large Language Model (LLM) solve simple abstract reasoning problems? We explore this broad question through a systematic analysis of GPT on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) ( Chollet 2019 ) , a representative benchmark of abstract reasoning ability from limited examples in which solutions require some “core knowledge” of concepts such as objects, goal states, counting, and basic geometry.

arxiv-2404-07730.creator: 1 st Lukáš Kratochvíla
arxiv-2404-07730.description: Abstract Obstacle detection is one of the basic tasks of a robot movement in an unknown environment. The use of a LiDAR (Light Detection And Ranging) sensor allows one to obtain a point cloud in the vicinity of the sensor. After processing this data, obstacles can be found and recorded on a map.

arxiv-2406-00203.title: Quantum phase transition of infrared radiation
arxiv-2406-00203.creator: Bartosz Biadasiewicz, Wojciech Dybalski
arxiv-2406-00203.description: Abstract We describe a phase transition of infrared radiation, driven by quantum fluctuations, which takes place at the boundary of (the conformal diagram of) Minkowski spacetime. Specifically, we consider a family of states interpolating between the vacuum and the Kraus-Polley-Reents infravacuum.

arxiv-2503-19223.title: FACE SPOOFING DETECTION TECHNOLOGY USING DEEP LEARNING
arxiv-2503-19223.creator: Najeebullah, Maaz Salman, Zar Nawab Khan Swati
arxiv-2503-19223.description: Abstract Author Contributions Najeebullah and M.S. equally contributed to this work. *Correspondence should be addressed to Najeebullah and M.S. ( maz.zeesal@gmail.com and najuofazli@gmail.com ). Abstract Digital image spoofing has emerged as a significant security threat in biometric authentication systems, particularly those relying on facial recognition.

arxiv-2507-00311.title: Tidal Stretching and Compression in Black Bounce Backgrounds
arxiv-2507-00311.creator: T. M. Crispim, Marcos V. de S. Silva, G. Alencar, Diego Sáez-Chillón Gómez
arxiv-2507-00311.description: Abstract Black bounces are compact objects that combine the structures of regular black holes with those of wormholes. These spacetimes exhibit a rich causal structure and can differ fundamentally from usual black holes. In this work, we study the behavior of the tidal forces by considering different black bounce models.

arxiv-2602-03019.title: FedKRSO: Communication and Memory Efficient Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models Thanks: G. Yang and T. Wu contributed equally to this work. Y. Sun and Y. arxiv-2602-03019.creator: Guohao Yang ∗ \ast , Tongle Wu ⋆ \star , Yuanxiong Guo ∗ \ast , Ying Sun ⋆ \star , and Yanmin Gong ∗ \ast
arxiv-2602-03019.description: Abstract Fine-tuning is essential to adapt general-purpose large language models (LLMs) to domain-specific tasks. As a privacy-preserving framework to leverage decentralized data for collaborative model training, Federated Learning (FL) is gaining popularity in LLM fine-tuning, but remains challenging due to the high cost of transmitting full model parameters and computing full gradients on resource-constrained clients.

pmc-11360711.title: Web-based objective and structured assessment of point-of-care lung ultrasound skills in resource-limited settings
pmc-11360711.creator: Veronique Suttels, Ines Chichignoud, Prudence Ablo Wachinou, Jacques Daniel Du Toit, Pierre-André Mans, Juan Manuel Blanco, Gildas Agodokpessi, Thomas Brahier, Mary-Anne Hartley, Elena Garcia, Noémie Boillat-Blanco
pmc-11360711.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundObjective assessment of skills after training is essential for safe implementation of lung point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS). In low-and middle-income countries (LMIC) there is a need for assessment tools without onsite experts to scale up POCUS access. Our objective is to develop a web-based assessment tool and evaluate trainees across different countries and at different time points after initial lung POCUS training.MethodsWe adapted the objective and validated lung ultrasound score (LUS-OSAUS) to a web-based tool with quiz and practical skills test.

pmc-11399229.title: Comprehensive comparison between vision transformers and convolutional neural networks for face recognition tasks
pmc-11399229.creator: Marcos Rodrigo, Carlos Cuevas, Narciso García
pmc-11399229.description: This paper presents a comprehensive comparison between Vision Transformers and Convolutional Neural Networks for face recognition related tasks, including extensive experiments on the tasks of face identification and verification. Our study focuses on six state-of-the-art models: EfficientNet, Inception, MobileNet, ResNet, VGG, and Vision Transformers.

pmc-12422768.title: Brucellosis. A Rare Cause of Biliary Dysplasia and Ampullary Adenocarcinoma?
pmc-12422768.creator: Zachary Vinton, Kevin Wolfe, Sean MacBride, Thomas Heffron, Vimal Jhaveri, Andrea K. Sotelo, Mark Rosenblatt, Clark Kulig, Matthew Stotts
pmc-12422768.description: Brucellosis, a zoonotic bacterial infection often characterized by nonspecific symptoms including fever, night sweats, and weight loss, has a prolonged and recurrent course, often leading to chronic symptoms if inadequately treated. Hepatic involvement is well-documented with manifestations ranging from mild hepatitis to hepatic abscesses and granulomas.

pmc-12524967.title: The Diagnostic Potential of Urinary Titin Fragment in Neuromuscular Diseases
pmc-12524967.creator: Andrea Sipos, Dávid Varga, Endre Pál
pmc-12524967.description: Biomarkers are important for the diagnosis and follow-up of neuromuscular diseases. Creatine kinase (CK) is a widely used marker of active muscle damage; however, it is not suitable for assessing muscle mass loss. Therefore, additional biomarkers are required to monitor skeletal muscle damage and loss. Titin plays an essential role in the structure and function of muscle fibers.

pmc-12708505.title: Advances in semi-rational design of terpene synthases and their modifying enzymes
pmc-12708505.creator: Xiqin Liang, Bengui Fan, Jun Wang, Yuan Qin, Tongle Yu, Pengpeng Xu, Guoli Wang, Tianyue An, Sixin Chen
pmc-12708505.description: As research on natural terpene compounds advances, their pharmacological properties and commercial potential are increasingly recognized. Microbial cell factories offer an efficient means of producing high-value terpene natural products through biosynthesis. However, inherent limitations of native enzymes, such as low catalytic activity and poor stability, have constrained further improvements in production capacity.

pmc-12768293.title: “Now you’re talking my language” - Improving health literacy and patient-directed knowledge of scientific abstracts through provision of plain language summaries created by artificial intelligence: A cross sectional infodemiology study
pmc-12768293.creator: John E. Moore, Beverley C. Millar
pmc-12768293.description: SCIENTIFIC ABSTRACT (Author Written)BackgroundDue to free and digital availability of scientific abstracts in medical journals, as well as search engines including PubMed, many patients are increasingly looking to these as reliable and trusted sources of information, amidst an information ecosystem of potential mis- and disinformation.

pmc-13227658.title: “We need to accept our limited resources”: a qualitative study exploring ambulance clinicians’ experiences of working conditions when caring for patients with breathlessness
pmc-13227658.creator: Wivica Kauppi, Karl Hedman, Hanna Maurin Söderholm, Magnus Andersson Hagiwara
pmc-13227658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBreathlessness is a common and potentially life-threatening symptom among patients and constitutes a frequent reason for ambulance dispatches. Within ambulance care, ambulance clinicians (ACs) are often required to make rapid clinical assessments and decisions under complex and unpredictable conditions. Despite this, there is limited knowledge of how ACs experience their working conditions in ambulance care when caring for patients with breathlessness.

pmc-13380423.title: Outcomes of Technically Optimal Intraoperative Radiation Therapy With Electrons Versus Whole-Breast External Beam Radiation in Suitable Patients With Breast Cancer
pmc-13380423.creator: Tanun Jitwatcharakomol, Jiraporn Setakornnukul, Suebwong Chuthapisith, Adune Ratanawichitrasin, Janjira Petsuksiri, Kullathorn Thephamongkhol
pmc-13380423.description: PurposeIntraoperative radiation therapy (IORT) with electrons is associated with higher rates of ipsilateral breast tumor recurrence in early-stage breast cancer than whole-breast external beam radiation therapy (EBRT). Although limited randomized and retrospective data suggest that this approach may suit a subset of patients, its role remains uncertain.

pmc-13425926.title: Metabolic disorder-MASLD-cardiovascular disease-kidney disease (MMCK) syndrome: an expansion of the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) framework
pmc-13425926.creator: Yan Guo, Ying Zhang, Suxuan Liu, Dajin Zou
pmc-13425926.description: BackgroundThe Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome framework acknowledges metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as a major manifestation, yet hepatic involvement remains insufficiently incorporated into risk stratification. This review proposes the metabolic disorder-MASLD-cardiovascular disease-kidney disease (MMCK) syndrome as an operational extension that integrates hepatic fibrosis assessment into cardiometabolic-renal care.

pmc-13538761.title: Durability and Safety of Imeglimin as an Add‐On to DPP‐4 Inhibitors in Japanese Type 2 Diabetes: The 104‐Week FAMILIAR Trial
pmc-13538761.creator: Masashi Shimoda, Takeshi Osonoi, Masahiro Iwamoto, Hideaki Kaneto, Kohei Kaku
pmc-13538761.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsTo evaluate the long‐term efficacy and safety of imeglimin added to dipeptidyl peptidase‐4 (DPP‐4) inhibitors in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes, focusing on glycemic durability and safety in elderly patients over 104 weeks.Materials and MethodsThis multicenter, randomized, placebo‐controlled trial comprised a 24‐week double‐blind phase (imeglimin 1000 mg or placebo twice daily) followed by an 80‐week open‐label extension in which all patients received imeglimin. Eligible patients had inadequate glycemic control despite DPP‐4 inhibitor monotherapy.

pmc-13588119.title: Distillation of a Locally Deployable 8B Language Model for Lung Histology Abstraction: A 33-Report Proof-of-Concept Study
pmc-13588119.creator: Dian Tri Wiyanti, Min-Huei Hsu, Daniel C A Nugroho
pmc-13588119.description: BackgroundThe manual data abstraction process for lung cancer registries is a labor-intensive undertaking that often results in registry lag. While cloud-based Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit high reasoning acuity, their reliance on third-party APIs poses significant data privacy risks and conflicts with institutional data sovereignty.
